evidence.V1: Three-quarter and top read clearly as an octagonal gem in a gold cup, but the front view and silhouette collapse into a rounded lidded-pot / cauldron blob (flat crown slab over a deep bowl, prongs read as small side nubs), so at 64 px it is only readable from some angles.
evidence.V2: Clear levels: big = teal crown + gold cup, medium = rolled rim lip and four prongs, small = crown top chamfer ring and facet planes; nothing reads as uniform noise.
evidence.V3: No correctness failure (A15 X/Y 0.0, gem aligned 0.0, all seats closed), but proportion is only partly stylised: the cup is nearly as tall as the gem and the prongs arc outward like pot handles and end on the pavilion below the girdle instead of gripping over the crown.
evidence.V4: Consistent soft bevels catch light: chamfer ring around the crown table (about 0.05 studs in top view), rounded rim lip, chamfered prong ends; only the crown/pavilion girdle is crisp, which suits a cut gem.
evidence.V5: Close-ups are clean: flat-shaded gem facets with no pinches, smooth gold cup and rim without seams or z-fighting; 0 flipped faces, 0 cap overlaps, 0 self-intersections (the 116 cross-shell overlaps are the intentional prong/gem/cup interpenetrations).
evidence.V6: Disciplined: gold accent plus one hue in three values (light crown table, mid crown sides, near-black pavilion); colourways (crimson, shadow) swap only the hue and keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 584 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500): at target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, kit gold matching the badge and potion anchors, one gem hue in up to three values, smooth-shaded gold with chamfers near 0.045 studs: fits the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a pickup/socket gem: origin bottom-centre, CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic.

artifacts: Not a shading artifact, but the arched prongs leave a visible open triangle between prong and gem (back-right prong in the setting close-up; pinholes beside both prongs in the silhouette), which makes them read as loose handles rather than claws.
top_fixes: Make the gem read as a gem from the front: give the crown a clearer table-and-facet profile (narrower table, steeper crown facets) and/or raise the gem / shorten the cup so the gem dominates the side silhouette instead of a pot-and-lid shape.
Reshape the four prongs into claws that run straight up the pavilion and fold over the girdle onto the crown edge, closing the arched gap so they visibly hold the stone.
Reduce the cup depth and flare slightly so the setting is a supporting medium form rather than half the object's height.
